claims.text: The premelting and melting behavior of Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu HEA nanoparticles is governed primarily by configurational-entropy stabilization of the solid-solution phase.
Configurational-entropy stabilization suppresses surface premelting in Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu HEA nanoparticles.
Configurational-entropy stabilization raises the HEA nanoparticle melting point above the weighted average for constituent pure-metal nanoparticles.
High chemical complexity and random atomic distributions reduce surface segregation relative to single-metal or bimetallic nanoparticles.
Reduced surface segregation decreases the tendency for local melting.
The initial Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu nanoparticles are consolidated solid solutions with random atomic distributions and uniform compositions.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the solid-solution phase.
Solid-solution stabilization reduces the likelihood of surface segregation and local melting.
Pure-metal nanoparticles exhibit surface-premelting phenomena that are suppressed in the proposed HEA nanoparticles.
Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu HEA nanoparticles will show a delayed onset of surface premelting relative to comparable pure-metal nanoparticles.
Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu HEA nanoparticles will have a higher melting point than the weighted average for size-matched Fe, Ni, Cr, Co, and Cu nanoparticles.
The HEA nanoparticle melting transition will be sharper than that of the pure-metal baseline.
HEA nanoparticles will exhibit less surface disorder before bulk melting than the pure-metal baseline.
Pure Fe, Ni, Cr, Co, and Cu nanoparticles typically exhibit pronounced surface premelting.
Pure-metal nanoparticles typically have melting points depressed relative to their bulk values.
The proposed mechanism applies to uniformly mixed, randomly distributed Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu solid-solution nanoparticles between 5 and 50 nm under inert atmosphere.
The proposed mechanism does not apply to phase-separated or core-shell particles or to particles in reactive environments.
Direct experimental evidence for the melting behavior of Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu HEA nanoparticles is lacking.
Prior relevant findings are limited to pure-metal and bimetallic nanoparticle systems.
